Title: Perodua QV-E: A much better deal than it was at launch
Article:
THE biggest improvement to Perodua QV-E since its Sepang debut a few months ago is not something you can see from behind the wheel.
It is the way Perodua has changed the ownership proposition.
When the QV-E first arrived in December 2025, the RM80,000 price tag looked attractive until you realised the 52.5-kWh battery was not included and had to be leased through a compulsory Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) arrangement.
Six months later, Perodua has effectively reset the equation: the QV-E can now be bought outright, battery included, for RM93,999, or RM69,999 with BaaS at RM215 a month.
A limited-time RM6,500 rebate brings those figures down to RM87,499 and RM63,499 respectively until Sept 30. That change matters because the QV-E itself was never the weak point of the package.
In fact, spending more time with Perodua's first EV makes its original pricing look even more unfortunate.
It Means Business
Underneath the angular body is a proper ground-up EV architecture developed with assistance from Magna Steyr, rather than an existing Daihatsu or Toyota platform converted to electric power.
The front-mounted motor produces 204 PS and 285 Nm, enough for a claimed 0-100 km/h time of 7.5 seconds.
The 52.5-kWh LFP battery gives it a 370-km WLTP range, while DC charging is rated at up to 60 kW.
On the road, the QV-E is therefore considerably more interesting than its humble Perodua badge might suggest.
The immediate response from the electric motor gives it the effortless acceleration you expect from an EV, but the car doesn't feel nervous or overpowered.
Its performance is particularly useful in Malaysian traffic, where the instant torque makes overtaking and joining faster-moving roads easy.
The steering has enough weight to make the car feel substantial, while the chassis is composed enough to give the QV-E a surprisingly mature feel.
This is perhaps the QV-E's biggest achievement: it doesn't drive like a cheap EV.
There are, however, compromises.
The suspension hardware is relatively straightforward, with MacPherson struts up front and a torsion beam at the rear.
The cabin also doesn't feel as spacious or versatile as you might expect from an electric vehicle designed from scratch.
Some of the interior execution falls short of the more polished Chinese EVs now competing for Malaysian buyers.
Yet there is something appealing about the QV-E's straightforwardness. Perodua hasn't tried to overwhelm the driver with screens and gimmicks.
Instead, the car's strongest qualities are its electric powertrain, safety equipment, compact dimensions and relatively uncomplicated driving experience.
It also carries a five-star Asean NCAP rating and includes useful features such as child presence detection, which monitors for movement inside the cabin after the vehicle is locked.
If it detects a child or occupant left behind, the QV-E can alert the driver through its warning system.
It is a thoughtful safety feature with real-world relevance.
Another neat touch is the QV-E's integration with Perodua's P-Go smartwatch.
Paired through the P-Circle ecosystem, the watch puts selected vehicle functions on the driver's wrist, complementing the smartphone app.
It adds a layer of convenience that feels particularly appropriate for Perodua's first EV, making everyday ownership feel more connected without relying entirely on the car's key fob.
More Local, Better Value
The more important story is what Perodua has done behind the scenes.
The company says a significant number of parts are now being manufactured locally, reducing dependence on overseas supply chains and improving parts availability.
Production has also increased to more than 500 units a month.
That localisation effort has allowed Perodua to pass some of the savings to customers. And that changes my view of the QV-E considerably.
At launch, it was difficult to recommend a car whose headline price didn't include its battery.
Today, the outright RM87,499 promotional price makes far more sense.
Even the BaaS version is easier to understand at RM63,499, particularly for buyers who prefer to avoid taking responsibility for long-term battery replacement and degradation.
Under BaaS, Perodua covers the battery for the nine-year term including protection, replacement and insurance.
There is still room for improvement.
The charging rate isn't particularly impressive by current EV standards, the interior could use more polish, and the rear packaging isn't its strongest attribute.
But these weaknesses are much easier to accept when the price is finally aligned with what the QV-E actually offers.
The QV-E is therefore a fascinating first attempt.
It isn't the most sophisticated EV in Malaysia, nor is it the most practical. But it is now a far more convincing proposition than the car that appeared at Sepang and subsequently went on sale.
Perodua has essentially fixed the QV-E's biggest problem without fundamentally changing the car.
The result is an EV that finally feels like it has found the price it should have had from the beginning.

Title: MCMC denies involvement in activities described in Anthropic report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has denied involvement in activities or arrangements described in a recent report by artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic.
In a statement, MCMC said it was aware of the report and took the matters raised seriously.
"For clarity, activities of the nature described in the report do not form part of MCMC's functions or mandate, and MCMC does not engage in such activities or arrangements."
Anthropic reported that Malaysia had been targeted in an AI-driven commercial manipulation operation involving more than 1,000 fake X accounts, voter data and constituency-based targeting systems aimed at influencing political sentiment.
The company, which operates the Claude AI platform, said it uncovered the operation after identifying an account that had used its
platform for election manipulation targeting Malaysian users.
According to Anthropic's report, Detecting and Countering Misuse of AI: September 2026, the platform was linked to an Istanbul-based technology company offering "influence-as-a-service" capabilities.
MCMC said it was examining the report and would seek further information and clarification from relevant parties to establish the facts and assess the matters raised.
It said any further action would be determined based on the information and evidence available and within its remit, in coordination with relevant authorities where necessary.
The commission said protecting the public and addressing online harms remained central to its responsibilities.
"MCMC will continue to preserve and ensure a safe and trusted online environment for Malaysia," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Widowed mother of four guts fish, collects boxes to feed children
Article:
ALOR STAR: A single mother of four has shared her heart-wrenching struggle to raise her family on a meagre income following the death of her husband to kidney cancer five years ago.
Nor Aza Hamzah, 44, said she frequently apologises to her youngest daughter for being unable to buy her a birthday cake due to financial hardship.
She said her 6-year-old daughter, Aimy Mariam, often cries after seeing her friends celebrate birthdays at school or eateries.
To support her children, Nor Aza takes on multiple odd jobs, including gutting catfish for RM3 a kg, collecting cardboard boxes along roadsides, and selling used cooking oil.
Her four children — Aqil Amjad, 13, Aina Aqila, 12, Alim Ajwad, 8, and Aimy Mariam, 6 — understand their situation, with some joining her to gather cardboard boxes during their free time.
"I am not ashamed to do this work as long as it earns money, but what I earn is barely enough for food and schooling expenses for my four children.
"When my youngest daughter cries asking for a cake and a party like her friends at kindergarten, it breaks my heart and leaves me in tears as well.
"She once asked why other children have fathers to celebrate their birthdays while she does not, which deeply saddened me," she said when met at the Cancer Community House (RKK) in Jalan Kanchut today.
Nor Aza said she prefers not to burden others and continues to live at her late husband's family home in Kepala Batas, Jitra.
Her daily routine revolves around taking her children to and picking them up from different schools, leaving her with limited time at home.
"After sending my children to school, I gut fish at the market and then collect boxes along roadsides or from rubbish bins.
"In the afternoon, I fetch the children from school, then resume collecting boxes and selling used cooking oil to earn money.
"I must earn money to keep going because my car frequently breaks down. That is the only vehicle I have to work and send my children to school," she said.
Despite the hardship, Nor Aza expressed gratitude that her children excel in their studies, calling it her greatest comfort.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Duopharma Biotech confirms cyberattack on it infrastructure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Duopharma Biotech Bhd has been hit by a cyberattack involving unauthorised access to its information technology (IT) infrastructure.
Preliminary investigations indicate that a set of data files had been exfiltrated, allegedly including personal data.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the pharmaceutical company said the incident was detected by its internal cyber defence systems, which identified an unauthorised system access attempt.
"Immediate containment protocols were successfully executed. To date, the core corporate network and internal operational systems are intact and remain fully secure and functional," it said.
Duopharma Biotech said that following the containment, the company initiated a comprehensive incident response review.
"Preliminary investigations have confirmed that there has been no disruption to our core business operations, and all corporate activities continue to function normally," it said.
The company said it will work with relevant internal and external cybersecurity specialists where necessary to conduct a digital forensic investigation and determine the exact scope of the files involved.
"The company's cyber security environment will also be reviewed and, if necessary, additional measures will be implemented to strengthen the security of the company's systems and data," it added.
The company believes there are no financial implications, while it continues to assess the impact as further information emerges from the ongoing investigation.
In relation to the alleged exfiltration of personal data, the company will notify the Personal Data Protection Commissioner within the prescribed timeframe.
"The company will continue to monitor the situation and may make further announcements should there be any material developments in relation to the incident," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 30 Malaysians arrested in Indonesia over alleged online scam syndicate
Article:
JAKARTA: Thirty Malaysians suspected of operating an online scam syndicate targeting their compatriots were arrested at a hotel in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, on Tuesday.
The suspects, comprising 22 men and eight women, were detained alongside a Taiwanese man at 11.15am during a joint operation between the local police and immigration authorities.
Pontianak Immigration Office chief Sam Fernando said the group occupied 14 hotel rooms to carry out their operations, which aimed to defraud Malaysian citizens. Initial investigations indicate no Indonesian nationals were targeted.
All 31 suspects were taken to the Pontianak Immigration Detention Centre for questioning, where several items linked to the illegal activity were seized.
Sam said three of the Malaysians had overstayed their visas, while others had violated the terms of their stay permits.
He added that the suspects had arrived separately via Pontianak airport, the Entikong land border crossing, and Jakarta, using various entry permits. Their length of stay ranged from three weeks to two months.
Indonesian authorities will coordinate with their Malaysian counterparts as investigations continue.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: German tourist dies after fall during Mount Jasar hike
Article:
CAMERON HIGHLANDS: A 58-year-old German tourist died after falling while hiking up Mount Jasar with his wife today.
Jorg Habelbusch was trekking with his wife, Marina Dehne, 57, when the incident occurred at 11.30am.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department public relations officer Zulfadli Zakaria said 16 personnel from the Cameron Highlands station were deployed after receiving an emergency call at 12.04pm.
Firefighters took more than an hour to navigate a steep trail to reach the site near the mountain peak.
"The victim fell into a ravine along a former water channel near the summit. Upon arrival, search personnel found him unconscious, and medical officers confirmed his death at the scene," Zulfadli said.
Rescue personnel, assisted by police, Civil Defence Force personnel, and Cameron Highlands Forestry Office officers, carried the body down a dangerous slope amid heavy rain, taking nearly three hours.
Dehne said she and her husband began their hike at 10am.
"My husband fell while stepping onto a slope. His face was buried in the mud, and another hiker tried to help lift him, but failed," she said.
The couple had arrived in Cameron Highlands yesterday for a three-day holiday.
The body was sent to the Sultanah Hajjah Kalsom Hospital for a post-mortem examination.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Petronas, Jogmec strengthen LNG collaboration via master agreement
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas LNG Ltd (PLL) has entered into a Master Sales and Purchase Agreement (MSPA) with the Japan Organisation for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC) to safeguard Japan's energy security while respecting Malaysia's domestic supply needs.
JOGMEC is a Japanese government agency operating under the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI), with responsibilities that include implementing Japan's energy and natural resources policies.
Petronas executive vice president and chief executive officer of gas and maritime business, Datuk Adif Zulkifli, said this agreement reflects the strength of the trust Petronas have built with JOGMEC over many years.
"By establishing a more agile framework for future liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply arrangements, we are better positioned to respond to evolving energy needs and contribute to greater supply resilience," he said in a statement today.
According to the statement, the MSPA reflects Petronas' ongoing commitment to delivering reliable energy solutions and fostering strategic partnerships that contribute to a secure, sustainable and resilient energy future.
The framework reinforces Petronas' role as a reliable and trusted LNG supplier to Japan and underscores the shared commitment to ensure reliable energy supplies amid an evolving global energy landscape.
The MSPA, signed during the LNG Producer and Consumer Conference 2026 (LNGPCC 2026), reflects the long-standing energy partnership between Petronas and Japan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rosmah touched by "Rindu saya ka?" Najib cutout at Umno general assembly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor said she was touched by an Umno supporter who brought a life-sized cutout of her husband, former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, to the Umno general assembly today.
In a Facebook post, Rosmah said the gesture by the supporter, known as "Mr J", reflected the longing among Najib's supporters for the former Umno president.
"Many miss Datuk Seri Najib, and so does our family.
"Feelings of disappointment are inevitable because we moved forward with great hope.
"But there is only so much we can do," she said.
In the clip, Mr J was seen carrying the cutout around the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, giving supporters a chance to pose for photographs of the Najib cutout.
"Datuk Seri Najib is on the way to PWTC," said Mr J to those missing the former prime minister.
The cutout also came with a speech bubble reading: "Hai! Rindu saya ka?" (Hi! Do you miss me?).
Rosmah said she was told Mr J had made the standee himself as his own way of coping with missing the former prime minister.
"We are deeply touched by what he did. Thank you, young man.
"Tomorrow, when I go to Kajang to visit my husband, I will tell him about this," she said.
The 2026 Umno general assembly, which began on Sept 9, runs until Sept 12.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Southern Score bags RM180mil Melaka hospital job
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Southern Score Builders Bhd has secured a RM180 million contract to undertake the main building works for a private hospital development in Bukit Katil, Melaka.
The contract covers constructing a seven-storey private hospital, a three-storey car park, a mechanical and electrical utility building, a pump house, a waste house and a VIE tank facility.
The scope also includes mechanical and electrical installations, external works, aluminium and glazing, interior fit-out works for common areas, facade treatment and lighting, kitchen equipment, landscaping, signage and a link bridge to a therapeutic garden, among others.
Work is scheduled to begin on Oct 15, 2026, with a contract period of 19 months and completion targeted for May 14, 2028.
Southern Score said the contract is expected to contribute to its net assets and earnings per share starting from the financial year ending June 30, 2027.
The project is a related-party transaction because the siblings of Southern Score director and major shareholder Tan Sri Datuk Seri Gan Yu Chai are the director and major shareholder of Radium Development Bhd.
The latter is the ultimate holding company of Radium Hospital Ayer Keroh Sdn Bhd.
Southern Score director Datuk Sydney Lim Tau Chin is also a non-independent non-executive director of Radium and holds less than one per cent of its equity.
The company said it had obtained shareholders' mandate for recurrent related-party transactions with Radium and its subsidiaries, associates and joint venture companies at its annual general meeting on Dec 9, 2025.
The company said the contract was entered into in the ordinary course of business and does not require approval from shareholders or any regulatory authorities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Finas to tighten filming permit rules to ensure content compliance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) will introduce additional conditions for filming permits to ensure productions comply with content guidelines and do not harm society.
Finas said the move was among three agreements reached during a meeting with the Malaysian Islamic Development Department (Jakim) today to strengthen governance of film and television content.
The additional conditions will be incorporated into the Filming Authentication Certificate (SPP) issued by Finas, requiring producers to consider religious sensitivities, cultural values, public interest and the country's legal framework.
The agency said the measures were not intended to restrict creative freedom, but to ensure creativity was developed responsibly.
Meanwhile, dramas titled Madu atau Racun and Cela will proceed to the next stage, with Jakim to conduct a panel assessment based on the overall storyline and content in accordance with the relevant guidelines.
Madu Atau Racun faced public backlash after controversial scenes depicting an intimate same-sex relationship between the female leads went viral.
It was reported that 12 episodes of the drama must be edited and resubmitted to Finas for further evaluation before the series can resume streaming.
Finas chief executive officer Datuk Azmir Saifuddin Mutalib said the six episodes already released must first be temporarily removed from iQIYI while the editing process is completed and an official decision is reached.
Finas and Jakim, together with relevant agencies, will also hold an engagement session with film and television industry players to discuss governance as well as guidelines for content production.
Finas said the initiatives reflected efforts to strengthen content governance while maintaining a balance between creative expression and societal sensitivities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: George Kent partners AI firm to expand tech footprint in Asean
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: George Kent (Malaysia) Bhd is strengthening its technology footprint through a collaboration between its wholly-owned GK SuperTech Sdn Bhd and Shandong Extreme Vision Technology Co Ltd.
The latter is a Hong Kong-listed artificial intelligence (AI) technology company.
The collaboration gives GK SuperTech exclusive rights to rebrand, market, distribute and sell Extreme Vision's AI algorithms and large models in Malaysia and Singapore.
The companies will also work together to deploy enterprise-level AI solutions and pursue opportunities across the wider Asean market.
The partnership was formalised through a binding term sheet covering the commercial deployment of Extreme Vision's proprietary AI technologies and its regional market expansion.
Extreme Vision specialises in AI-powered computer vision algorithms and large models that enable machines to interpret and analyse visual data in real time.
Its technologies are used in areas including smart cities, smart manufacturing, industrial automation, infrastructure monitoring and public safety.
As part of the collaboration, George Kent's manufacturing plant in Puchong, Selangor will serve as a pilot site for implementing Vision AI.
The facility will showcase the application of advanced AI technologies in a manufacturing environment, aiming to establish a benchmark for smart manufacturing.
George Kent executive chairman Tan Sri Tan Kay Hock said the collaboration marked a significant step in the group's expansion into Agentic AI technology.
"This collaboration provides GK SuperTech with a clear pathway to bring advanced AI solutions to Malaysia and Singapore, while creating opportunities for further growth across Asean," he said.
He said the collaboration also supported the objectives of Malaysia's National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 to accelerate AI adoption across industries.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Single mother fined RM1,800 for assaulting man at Melaka Sentral
Article:
MELAKA: A single mother of four was fined RM1,800 by the Ayer Keroh magistrate's court today after pleading guilty to assaulting a man at an eatery in Melaka Sentral in July.
Magistrate Sharda Shienha Mohd Suleiman imposed the sentence on Nurul Amalina Mohamad Kamal, 32, after taking into account her guilty plea, mitigation, the facts of the case and the prosecution's submission on sentencing.
Amalina was charged with voluntarily causing hurt to Mohd Zubir Maarof, 47, together with four other people who had previously been charged.
She was charged under Section 323 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same Code, which carries a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both, upon conviction.
Based on the facts of the case, the victim was punched and kicked by the accused while they were discussing a case, resulting in injuries to his back, head and nose, as well as pain in his right ribs that made it difficult for him to breathe.
The incident was captured on closed-circuit television (CCTV), while mobile phone recordings and witnesses also showed the accused assaulting and injuring the victim.
National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer Muhammad Izzuddin Ab Malek, in mitigation, pleaded for a minimum fine, saying that Amalina was unemployed and a single mother of four.
"This is the accused's first offence.
"She has promised not to repeat it and will try to control her emotions and allow the authorities to resolve any issues that arise," he said.
Deputy public prosecutor S. Thiviya urged the court to impose a sentence that would serve as a lesson to the accused to control her emotions better and leave investigations to the relevant authorities.
The court then fined Amalina RM1,800, in default of two months' imprisonment. She paid the fine.
Earlier, a commotion broke out outside the courtroom between members of the media and a man who attempted to prevent the accused from being photographed by grabbing and pushing the hands of a journalist and videographer.
Amalina, who appeared surprised by the large media presence, was heard asking, "Wow, there are so many of you. Am I an artist? Any questions?" as she was escorted by police.
She also asked a friend to record members of the media covering the proceedings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Don't let rivals' narratives divide Umno, veterans warn
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno must not allow political pressure from its opponents to divide the party or turn its own members into conduits for narratives built by its rivals, said Veteran Umno.
Reading out their resolutions at the 2026 Umno General Assembly, the group's committee member Datuk Adam Abd Hamid said the party must remain united in facing political pressure and attacks.
"Umno must unite in facing the political pressure, intimidation and attacks carried out by Pakatan Harapan against the party and its leaders.
"We do not defend wrongdoing, but we must defend justice, transparent legal processes and a person's right not to be punished based on perception.
"As Umno grows stronger, the attacks will become more intense. That is why party unity is our most important line of defence," he said in his debate.
Adam said Umno should also lead efforts to realign Malay-Muslim political strength based on the Federal Constitution, the interests of the people and national stability.
He said such a realignment should not be based on hostility towards other races, but on consolidating political strength without compromising justice or the prosperity of a multiracial society.
Prolonged divisions, he said, will only weaken Malay bargaining power and create room for others to determine the country's political agenda.
"Umno must be the leader, not merely a complement, in shaping Malay political power," it said.
On Umno's relationship with Perikatan Nasional (PN), he called for strategic understanding and negotiations to avoid clashes that could split the Malay-Muslim vote.
He said cooperation with PN must be based on sincerity, mutual respect and recognition of Umno's strength and shared interests.
"On our relationship with PN, particularly Pas, I ask that we approach it through proper negotiations.
"Do not look only at the question of power. If we focus solely on power, eventually we will fight because we want the prime minister's post, and they want the prime minister's post. We want to retain our seats, and they will want to retain theirs. Unity cannot last long that way," he said.
Instead, he said both sides should focus on areas where cooperation could benefit the Malay community, particularly economic issues and food security.
He said through Umno's experience with PH, it showed that cooperation without sincerity, mutual respect and reciprocity will only weaken Umno's identity and position.
"PH cannot be regarded as a truly trustworthy partner as long as attacks, pressure and efforts to discredit Umno continue," he said.
He also called for veterans to be formally included in Umno's election machinery at national, state, division, state constituency and polling district levels.
Adam said the veterans' experience, community networks and relationships with traditional voters could complement technology-driven campaigning.
He further called for veterans to strengthen ties with non-governmental organisations, professional bodies, retirees' associations and community groups to rebuild public confidence in Umno.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Serian still tops API reading nationwide with 'very unhealthy' 220
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Serian had the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading as of 5.30pm today, rising to a very unhealthy 220 from 195 at 8am today.
Checks on the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) showed that 11 areas recorded unhealthy API levels — 10 in Sarawak and one in Johor.
They were Samarahan (186), Sri Aman (184), Kuching (180), Sarikei (160), Samalaju (158), Bintulu (157), Sibu (156), Mukah (154), Miri (152), ILP Miri (136) and Pasir Gudang, Johor (109).
Another 47 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings.
In Sabah, moderate readings were recorded in Kimanis at 96, Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (94), Kota Kinabalu (91), Keningau (63) and Sandakan (58).
Labuan recorded a moderate reading of 97, while Kapit (95) and Limbang (80) in Sarawak also remained in the moderate category.
In Johor, Larkin recorded a reading of 95, followed by Kota Tinggi (93), Segamat (91), Tangkak (87), Kluang (86) and Pengerang (85).
In Selangor, Johan Setia registered a reading of 99, followed by Kuala Selangor (79), Shah Alam (77), Klang (69), Petaling Jaya (67) and Banting (65).
In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded a reading of 78, followed by Batu Muda at 77 while Putrajaya stood at 67.
On the east coast, Kemaman in Terengganu registered a reading of 86 and Kuala Terengganu 60, while Kota Baru in Kelantan recorded a reading of 52.
Pahang's Indera Mahkota recorded 79, followed by Balok Baru, Kuantan (72), Jerantut (69), Rompin (67) and Temerloh (59).
In Perak, Tasek Ipoh and Seri Manjung both recorded 67, followed by Tanjung Malim (64) and Pegoh, Ipoh (59).
In Negri Sembilan, Seremban recorded (62) and Port Dickson (56).
Up north, Sungai Petani in Kedah recorded (57), while Seberang Jaya (54) and Minden (52) in Penang remained in the moderate category.
Meanwhile, nine areas recorded good air quality, mostly in the northern region.
These were Seberang Perai (49), Balik Pulau (37), Alor Star (35), Kulim Hi-Tech (38), Kangar (18) and Langkawi (18).
The remaining areas were Taiping (38), Besut (43) and Tanah Merah (42).
API readings of 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy and 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings exceeding 300 are hazardous.

Title: Citaglobal bags RM82.1mil residential college job
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Citaglobal Bhd has secured an RM82.1 million design-and-build subcontract for the new residential college at Institut Pendidikan Guru Bahasa Melayu here.
Citaglobal said its subsidiary Citaglobal Land Sdn Bhd accepted a letter of award from Purnama Base Sdn Bhd for the project.
"The fixed lump-sum subcontract is valued at RM82.12 million and is scheduled for delivery over 22 months, subject to the terms of the subcontract," it said in a statement.
Citaglobal said the project is part of a government development initiative in the education sector, implemented through the Public Works Department (JKR).
It noted that JKR is the employer under the main contract, while Purnama Base is the main contractor pursuant to a main contract with JKR dated Dec 30 2025.
The award further strengthens Citaglobal Land's track record in public sector infrastructure projects and leverages the company's integrated design, engineering and construction capabilities.
Following acceptance of the subcontract, Citaglobal's outstanding pro forma order book stood at RM1.5 billion as of June 30, 2026.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PTT Synergy buys Penang land for RM62.53mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PTT Synergy Group Bhd subsidiary PTT Logistics Hub 3 Sdn Bhd is buying a plot of freehold land in Seberang Perai Selatan, Penang for RM62.53 million.
In its filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said PTT Logistics signed a sale and purchase agreement (SPA) with Lee Mooi Khean for the acquisition.
The land will be held as an investment property, with potential for future development, aligning with the company's business expansion plans.
"The proposed acquisition is a strategic investment undertaken in line with the company's long-term growth and expansion objectives.
"By securing the land for future development and operational requirements, the proposed acquisition is expected to strengthen the company's asset base and facilitate the continued growth and expansion of its business over the medium to long term," it said.
PTT Synergy said the price was determined on a willing-buyer, willing-seller basis, after considering the acquisition's rationale and prospects, as well as indicative asking prices for comparable land in the surrounding area.
The RM62.53 million will be settled entirely in cash, funded through a combination of internally generated funds and bank borrowings.
PTT Synergy expects to complete the acquisition in the first quarter of 2027.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno grassroots open to closer Pas ties if it benefits the people
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno grassroots are unlikely to reject closer cooperation with Pas if it benefits the rakyat, said a Melaka Umno leader.
Duyong assemblyman Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem, who is also a deputy Melaka state executive councillor, said any potential cooperation between the two parties must be built around common ground without either side compromising its core principles.
He said both parties had several fundamental areas in common, including the rights of Malays and Bumiputera, the institution of the Malay Rulers and the sovereignty of Islam.
"Previously, Umno was on one straight line and Pas was on another. Both sides need to move slightly towards each other without compromising their principles.
"They need to find a point of convergence, and that is where a bigger joint effort can take shape," he said when met today at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here.
However, Noor Helmy said it was too early to determine whether such cooperation would translate into a formal political pact ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16).
He said Malaysia's political landscape was highly dynamic and the most suitable arrangement could differ from one state to another.
Political cooperation, he said, should therefore not be viewed solely through the lens of a national arrangement, particularly given the differing political strengths and dynamics across states.
He added that a Pas-led government might be acceptable in states such as Kelantan, Kedah, Perlis and Terengganu, but Melaka had a different political landscape.
"Johor has its own formula, Negri Sembilan has its own formula and Melaka has its own. We do not yet know which formula will be the most suitable for GE16," he said.
"As long as there is cooperation, it is not necessarily about who becomes the chief minister. What matters is how it is arranged so that everyone feels comfortable," he added.
His remarks came amid renewed discussion at the assembly on Malay unity and the possibility of closer ties between Umno and Pas, with the party leadership stressing the importance of strengthening Umno while remaining open to cooperation with other Malay-based parties.
Noor Helmy also said any cooperation should not weaken Umno's ability to stand independently.
"Political cooperation is a political strategy. A coalition is a bonus. Umno must be prepared to stand on its own feet, regardless of whether there is a coalition," he said.

Title: IHH maintains claim on Fortis losses, respects court decision
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IHH Healthcare maintains its claim that it suffered losses due to delays in obtaining the mandatory tender offer approvals required for its acquisition of Fortis Healthcare.
These delays arose from the dispute between Daiichi Sankyo Co Ltd and its judgment debtors. IHH and its indirect wholly owned subsidiary Northern TK Venture Pte Ltd (NTK) were unrelated parties to that dispute.
IHH said in a statement that the group and NTK respected the judgment issued by the Tokyo District Court on Sept 10.
NTK is reviewing the judgment in detail with its legal counsel and will carefully consider its available legal options.
NTK remains committed to protecting its rights and interests through the appropriate legal channels, the group added.
IHH-NTK's acquisition of Fortis in 2018 was undertaken through a transparent, publicly disclosed and fully regulated process, the group said.
The transaction received all necessary corporate, shareholder and regulatory approvals, including those required under the Competition Commission of India and SEBI takeover regulations.
On Thursday, the Tokyo District Court reportedly dismissed all claims brought by NTK against Daiichi Sankyo.
NTK filed a claim in October 2023, alleging that the Japanese drugmaker caused it losses by preventing it from proceeding with open offers to acquire additional shares in the Indian hospital chain in 2018.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five killed in Thursday's Dutch coach crash in Switzerland
Article:
GENEVA: Five people were killed when a coach carrying Dutch tourists in eastern Switzerland crashed this week, police said on Friday.
The accident happened on Thursday afternoon in the eastern canton of Graubunden.
The coach hit a safety barrier before overturning and plunging down an embankment, a local police spokesman told Swiss media on Thursday.
The Dutch Federation of Travel Agencies (ANVR) told AFP that the coach belonged to the tour company Oad and was carrying 48 passengers, all of them from the Netherlands.
According to the ANVR, the coach left the Netherlands on Monday and was on a day trip to Switzerland from Austria when the crash happened.
Zernez is the entry point for visitors to the Swiss national park, a vast Alpine reserve stretching more than 100 square kilometres (40 square miles) across the mountainous Engadine valley.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's disaster expertise sought by global resilience coalition
Article:
NEW DELHI: Malaysia should join the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) to share its expertise in managing natural disasters, says its director-general Amit Prothi.
CDRI director-general Amit Prothi said Malaysia, as an Asean member, had extensive experience in dealing with disasters including landslides, tsunamis and major earthquakes.
He said the coalition was keen to strengthen cooperation with Asean countries and regional organisations, including the Asean Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management (AHA Centre) in Indonesia.
"Many countries in Asean have been working on the disaster-resilient infrastructure agenda for a long time, and we very much want to build partnerships with them.
"Vietnam is already a member, while the Philippines will become a member tomorrow. So, I hope more countries from Asean will join us," he said.
Prothi was speaking during a briefing for an international media delegation hosted by India's External Affairs Ministry in New Delhi and Mumbai today.
The visit was organised as part of the Indian government's initiatives ahead of the 18th BRICS Summit, which will be held in New Delhi this weekend.
Malaysia is participating in the BRICS Leaders' Summit as a BRICS partner country.
The CDRI was initiated by the Indian government and formally launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the United Nations Climate Action Summit in New York in September 2019.
The coalition focuses on strengthening infrastructure such as roads, bridges, hospitals, water supply systems and electricity grids to withstand the impact of climate change and natural disasters.
Its work covers risks including floods, earthquakes, tsunamis and landslides, while also providing a platform for member countries to exchange technology, research findings, technical standards and post-disaster recovery practices.
It also helps developing countries and highly vulnerable areas, including small island nations, gain access to international financing and expertise to upgrade infrastructure following disasters.
Prothi said Malaysia would be a valuable addition to the coalition given its experience in managing climate-related risks.
"At the same time, the risk of natural disasters is increasing in every country. In Malaysia, for example, floods are a major problem.
"If you look at major urban areas such as Kuala Lumpur and Melaka, flooding is an issue. Extreme heat is also beginning to pose a challenge.
"For me, it would be very good if Malaysia joined us. The expertise and experience you have can be shared with other countries and also brought back to benefit your own country," he said.
Prothi said Asean's collective experience in disaster management could also benefit other countries facing similar challenges.
He cited Colombia, which recently experienced a major earthquake and sought CDRI's advice on rebuilding damaged infrastructure.
"That kind of experience is available in countries such as Indonesia and the Philippines," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hextar Industries RM177.48 mln woodpeckers deal falls through
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hextar Industries Bhd's proposed acquisition of a 51 per cent equity interest in Woodpeckers Group Sdn Bhd for RM177.48 million in cash has fallen through after certain conditions for the deal were not fulfilled.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Hextar Industries said the conditional share purchase agreement (SPA) entered into between the company and the vendors on Feb 12, 2026, had lapsed today.
It said the SPA, subsequently varied and supplemented by a supplemental agreement dated June 23, 2026, had lapsed. Certain conditions precedent were not fulfilled within the conditional period.
"Accordingly, the proposed acquisition will not proceed," the company said.
The company made announcements relating to the proposed acquisition on Feb 12, June 12 and June 23, 2026.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno Overseas Club proposes emergency network for Malaysians abroad
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Umno Overseas Club has proposed setting up a community emergency response network to help Malaysian diplomatic missions assist citizens abroad during crises.
Newcastle Umno Overseas Club president Muhammad Amir Ikram Mohd Fadil said the network could link Malaysian communities abroad with embassies and consulates to help identify citizens who needed urgent assistance.
He said the proposal was not intended to take over the role of Malaysian diplomatic missions, but to serve as a link between the missions and communities on the ground.
"We do not want to take over the duties of the embassy. We want to be a link between the embassy and the community on the ground.
"When an emergency happens, we want to quickly identify who needs help, who has young children and who has been cut off from food supplies," he said while debating the Umno president's policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Amir said Malaysian communities abroad were often better placed to identify the immediate needs of fellow Malaysians during emergencies because they were already present in affected areas.
He said a coordinated network would allow communities to respond more quickly while diplomatic missions handled official assistance and consular matters.
"Technology can tell us where we are. The embassy can provide assistance. But the community ensures that no one is left behind," he said.
He said Malaysians living overseas could face a range of unexpected emergencies, including geopolitical conflicts, airspace closures, cancelled flights and natural disasters.
"The world today is uncertain. Geopolitical conflicts can erupt within hours. Airspace can be closed, flights can be cancelled and natural disasters can happen," he said.
He also highlighted concerns over food supply disruptions and growing anti-Islam sentiment in some parts of the world as additional challenges faced by Malaysians abroad.
Amir said the government had already introduced measures such as the e-Konsular system, which allowed Malaysians overseas to register their whereabouts and helped facilitate assistance during emergencies.
He said the proposed community network could complement existing government systems by providing a stronger grassroots response.
He also called for Malaysian community facilities abroad, including Malaysia Halls, to be maintained and modernised as part of the country's support network for Malaysians overseas.
Amir said the Umno Overseas Club could play a greater role in connecting Malaysian communities with government agencies and ensuring that citizens abroad had avenues to seek assistance when needed.
"We must ensure that those who are far from home are not left to face these situations alone," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Vestland secures RM410mln contract for Jalan Ampang development
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Vestland Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary Vestland Resources Sdn Bhd (VRSB) has secured a RM410 million contract from Golden Armani Sdn Bhd for construction works in Jalan Ampang, Kuala Lumpur.
The development involves a 69-storey small office home office (SOHO) tower and a 78-storey small office versatile office (SOVO) tower.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the construction company said VRSB had accepted the letter of award to undertake superstructure works, landscaping, facilities floor, façade lighting, signages and miscellaneous works for the development.
"The scope of works includes the design, approval, construction, completion, testing and commissioning of the related works.
"The contract will commence on Sept 15, 2026, and is scheduled to be completed on Sept 14, 2029," it said.
Vestland said the contract is expected to contribute positively to the earnings and net assets of the company and its subsidiaries.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar departs for India to attend 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has departed for New Delhi, India, to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit.
During his visit, Anwar is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
He will also visit Keralam, where he is expected to meet India's Grand Mufti Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad to exchange views on community development, education and religious affairs.
"After completing the diplomatic mission in India, I will proceed to Male, Maldives, for an official visit at the invitation of President Dr Mohamed Muizzu," he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar expressed hope that the visits would bring tangible benefits to the people and the country.
The summit, themed "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability", will focus on strengthening resilience and economic cooperation, as well as trade and investment reforms.
Leaders are also expected to discuss intra-BRICS cooperation on common priorities and exchange views on global and regional issues of mutual importance.
The summit will bring together leaders of BRICS member and partner countries, as well as outreach invitees.
Among the leaders expected to attend are Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zoo Negara says all animals safe after flash floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Flash floods at Zoo Negara two days ago were triggered by persistent heavy rain that caused water from Sungai Pandan and Sungai Kemensah in Hulu Klang to converge and overflow.
Zoo Negara deputy president Datuk Rosly Lana said none of the animals were injured or killed despite floodwaters reaching up to 1.2min several areas.
He also dismissed claims by some visitors that the zoo had failed to assist the animals during the floods, saying the severity of the flooding made it impossible for vehicles to access the affected areas.
"The floodwaters were flowing too fast, and no vehicles could get through.
"Even the trams could not enter as the reptile, hippo and savannah areas were inundated," he said.
Rosly said water from the two rivers quickly overflowed into several animal enclosures, affecting routes used by visitors and staff.
He said some animals, including the hippos, were unaffected because of their natural behaviour.
"That is the hippo area, and they naturally like being submerged in water, so they had no problems," he said.
"All the other animals are safe. The enclosures have also been cleaned since two days ago.
"There was quite a lot of thick mud, but the situation was fully resolved within two hours," he said.
Rosly said the zoo handled the situation better than during previous major floods, with no animal fatalities reported.
He added that cleaning and monitoring efforts were continuing to ensure the animals' safety and visitors' comfort.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Exorcism' murder: Court acquits healer who suffered from schizophrenia
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Driven by grief after losing her youngest child, a former beautician turned traditional healer fell deeper into delusion, eventually believing her deceased child had possessed her to grant her spiritual healing powers.
That mental collapse culminated on a July evening in 2022 inside an Ampang home, when a ritual meant to "exorcise a ghost" ended in a brutal killing.
The High Court acquitted 55-year-old Che Hong Chiew of murdering her client, 41-year-old Lim Sin Hue, after ruling that Che was of unsound mind during the violent episode.
Judicial Commissioner Suriyati Hasimah Mohd Hashim found that Che was suffering from schizophrenia at the time, leaving her unable to understand the nature or consequences of her actions.
Instead of sentencing Che to death or jail, the court ordered her to be detained at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak at the pleasure of the Sultan of Selangor.
The prosecution has appealed against the ruling.
The tragic encounter began when Lim, who suffered from severe abdominal pain and believed that a baby was inside her stomach, was introduced to Che by a friend.
Lim agreed to undergo a week-long Buddhist healing ritual at Che's residence in Pandan Perdana, Ampang.
However, when Lim and her mother went to Che's house on July 27, 2022, the horror began to unfold.
Locked inside the home to prevent "disruption," Lim's mother looked on as Che lay on top of her daughter, punching her chest, biting her private parts, and stomping on her abdomen.
As she recited mantras, Che pressed a hot, steaming bowl directly against Lim's neck and mouth.
When Lim's mother tried to intervene, Che warned her to stay back, insisting the violent beatings were necessary to drive out a "demonic disturbance" residing in the victim's stomach.
The intensity of the assault left Lim immobilised and unable to scream.
Sometime around 5pm, Che told Lim's mother that the 41-year-old had died, and apologised. She promised she would take care of the grieving mother for the rest of her life.
Che then washed and dressed Lim's body, claiming that her spiritual "sifu" (master) and the police were on their way.
A subsequent post-mortem examination showed that Lim had died from severe blunt force trauma, suffering multiple abrasions and bruises to her face, chest, abdomen and upper and lower limbs, as well as numerous broken ribs.
During the trial, the court heard how Che's life spiralled out of control following the death of her youngest child in an accident, which was further compounded by a 2018 divorce.
The mother of two then began spending long hours at a local temple and, over time, became convinced she could see, hear, and speak to her late child.
Around a month before the fatal incident, Che believed her child had possessed her body, granting her the ability to see spirits and cure possessed individuals.
When treating Lim using a mix of mantras, herbal massage, cupping, and gua sha, Che claimed two spirits took over her body and mind, giving her a surge of energy and strength.
She maintained that she only realised something was wrong when Lim suddenly stopped moving or breathing.
Psychiatric expert Dr. Isabel Shamini David testified that Che had schizophrenia and was actively delusional during the assault, though her condition could be stabilised through medication and psychiatric care.
In her grounds of judgment, the judicial commissioner noted that while direct and circumstantial evidence proved Lim died at Che's hands, Che's mind was profoundly fractured by years of unaddressed trauma.
"Her unstable mental state had persisted for a long time, stemming from the death of her youngest child, which led to depression and social withdrawal, compounded by a divorce," Suriyati said.
"These circumstances placed a heavy emotional strain on her, ultimately resulting in a diagnosis of schizophrenia."
"Her intention was to remove what she believed to be a ghost from Lim's stomach, rather than to kill her," she said.
The court concluded that Che truly believed she was driving a ghost from Lim's abdomen and lacked any intention or realization that her physical assault would result in death.
Deputy public prosecutor Ainul Mardiyah Mohd Ali appeared for the prosecution, while Che was represented by Datuk Geethan Ram Vincent and Jeremiah Anand.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno must secure written agreements to prevent betrayal in political cooperation, says delegate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno must secure written agreements to safeguard its interests in future political cooperation and guard against another betrayal, said Perlis delegate Datuk Dr Fathul Bari Mat Jahya.
Fathul Bari, who is Kangar Umno division chief, urged the leadership to prioritise the party's rights and political survival in negotiations, saying cooperation required sacrifice without compromising its dignity.
"This time, in any negotiations, put our rights and our survival first.
"Let the negotiations be formalised in a written agreement so there will be no more betrayal, although we know betrayal can still happen," he said while debating the Umno president's policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Fathul said bargaining was part of political negotiations and Umno should not hesitate to assert its rights.
Referring to party president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's earlier remarks on the government's branding, he said promises did not always translate into the agreed outcome.
"We were promised a National Unity Government, but what we got was Madani.
"One thing was promised, but the outcome was different. That is the reality," he said.
Earlier, Zahid questioned changes to the coalition government's name, saying the agreed
Malaysia Unity Government
name had evolved into National Unity Government before becoming the Madani government.
He urged that his proposed "Grand Collaboration" be built on mutual understanding.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia needs extensive EV policy to spur localisation, not just higher taxes: Experts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia should take lessons from Thailand's higher tax policy on completely built-up (CBU) electric vehicles (EV) but industry experts caution that simply raising taxes will not be enough to drive meaningful localisation.
Automotive analyst Shamsul Yunos said Thailand's use of tax pressure had helped push automakers towards local production, while Malaysia had traditionally taken a more measured approach.
"The real question is whether our pace [in vendor development] is too slow given how fast the market is moving," he told the Business Times.
On Thursday, reports said that Thailand's EV board had approved plans to raise excise taxes on imported EVs in a bid to stimulate investment in its domestic automotive manufacturing sector.
Imported units will be subjected to higher duty rates exceeding the existing 10 per cent excise duty threshold, while those produced domestically utilizing local components would qualify for the most favorable tax rates.
The final tax figures are expected to be finalized by month-end, Thailand finance ministry permanent secretary Lavaron Sangsnit was reported as saying.
Shamsul said Malaysia's shift away from blanket tax exemptions for imported EVs was a necessary move, as continued reliance on CBU vehicles could worsen the country's automotive trade deficit without generating sufficient domestic economic value.
He said Malaysia needed to ensure that any policy aimed at promoting local assembly also resulted in deeper domestic participation, including component manufacturing, technology and research and development.
"The ballooning automotive trade deficit is the elephant in the room when it comes to Malaysia's EV push.
"When you have a massive wave of fully imported vehicles flooding the market, the money just flows right back out, and consumer adoption alone is not going to build a sustainable local industry," he said.
Meanwhile, Wattz Mobility Sdn Bhd chief financial officer Dr Muhammad Safiuddin Rosli said Malaysia could consider stronger differentiation in tax treatment between CBU and completely knocked-down (CKD) EVs, but any tax changes would need to be carefully calibrated.
Safiuddin said for local assembly to generate genuine economic value, CKD criteria must enforce meaningful local content rules (such as local vendor integration requirements) rather than serving as simple kits for bolt-on assembly.
"Therefore, any increase in CBU excise taxation must be carefully calibrated alongside fuel subsidy rationalization and strict local vendor contribution thresholds to ensure local assembly remains economically viable and competitive," he said.
On the same note, industry specialist Hezeri Samsuri said Malaysia also needed to strengthen incentives for local automotive vendors if it wanted to replicate Thailand's success in building a domestic manufacturing ecosystem.
Hezeri said incentives should be provided not only to vehicle manufacturers but also to local component suppliers, adding that Malaysia needed to clarify its ambition of becoming an EV hub in the region.
"I think the numbers have shown that Thailand knows better at this. The government should sit down and come up with a long term plan because right now, we can see that Malaysia is losing many local vendors.
"We are now down to only one automotive tyre factory in Taiping, which means we have to import them into Malaysia. There are no clear incentives given to promote local vendors," he said.
From the consumer and charging infrastructure perspective, Amtech EV founder and managing director Muhammad Hafiy Isyraf Mohd Rosli said Malaysia was already moving towards a more mature EV market, although higher vehicle prices resulting from changes in incentives could affect adoption in the short term.
However, Hafiy said the long-term direction of EV adoption remained positive, with the company seeing increasing demand for home charging installations.
"We should not measure the success of the EV industry simply by how many EVs we sell. We should also look at how much value we are creating around the entire ecosystem.
"For example, charging infrastructure, electrical components, installation and maintenance, software, energy management, technical training and skilled jobs are all areas where Malaysian companies can play a bigger role," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] All southbound lanes reopened after North-South Expressway landslide
Article:
IPOH: All southbound lanes on the North-South Expressway (Plus) at Km263.6 have been fully reopened following a landslide earlier today, according to the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM).
However, traffic congestion stretched for 8km from the Menora Tunnel towards Ipoh Utara following the incident.
The landslide initially blocked the left lane, forcing a complete closure to allow authorities to carry out clearing operations and safety inspections.
LLM reported that congestion originally stretched for 4km before worsening to 8km by 5.15pm.
Travel navigation apps estimated delays of around 40 minutes through the affected stretch, while closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed active slope clearing works at the site.
LLM advised road users to exercise caution while driving in rainy weather. The exact cause of the landslide has yet to be determined.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KL DOE warns of fake procurement scams after two suppliers lose more than RM200,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — The Kuala Lumpur Department of Environment (DOE) has detected several attempts by irresponsible parties to commit fraud using the department’s name.
Its Director, Sharifah Zakiah Syed Sahab, said that as of today, eight such cases have been detected involving government procurement order scams, resulting in losses totalling more than RM200,000 for two suppliers.
She said her department first detected the scam on September 4, when a representative of a diving equipment supplier came to the department to verify the authenticity of government procurement documents.
“Prior to that, KL DOE also received several inquiries regarding these government procurement documents starting in mid-August, and last Tuesday (September 8) from a supplier company representative who also came to inquire about a souvenir order worth more than RM100,000 supposedly made by KL DOE for an upcoming programme,” she told Bernama, here today.
She noted that checks by her department revealed that the department had never made any souvenir orders or programme bookings. Instead, the orders were made using forged documents that abused officers’ names, alongside fake letterheads and management signatures.
“Based on the suppliers’ information, they claimed to have transferred more than RM100,000 to certain parties as an advance payment for the souvenirs, and KL DOE has asked the suppliers to make a police report regarding the scam,” she said.
Elaborating further, she added that KL DOE also lodged a police report last Wednesday denying the involvement of department officers in the incident, while reports were also made to the DOE Headquarters Finance Division.
However, she mentioned that yesterday and today, her department still received inquiries regarding the fake procurement orders.
“In fact, today there was a supplier who was scammed with losses exceeding RM100,000, and the department has subsequently referred these cases further to the Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department,” she said.
Sharifah Zakiah also advised all suppliers and contractors to be cautious and verify the authenticity of any government procurement documents they received. — Bernama

Title: Fire Dept: Two men found dead in separate incidents in Penang drain and Perak river
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Sept 11 — Two men were found dead in separate incidents in Penang and Perak today, one in a drain near a school here and the other in Sungai Perak.
The body of Ooi Chai Siang, 37, was found in a drain about 1.5 metres deep near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Tun Hussein Onn in Taman Kelisa Emas here today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received a call from the police at 12.10pm requesting assistance to retrieve the body.
“A team from the Perai Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) proceeded to the location and, upon arrival, found a man in the drain. The operation commander then instructed firefighters wearing full personal protective equipment (PPE) to retrieve the body,” he said in a statement today.
He said the body was handed over to the police for further action and later sent to the hospital for a post-mortem to determine the actual cause of death.
In Ipoh, the body of a 38-year-old man feared drowned after jumping into Sungai Perak to retrieve his boat, which had drifted away from a fish cage yesterday, was found this afternoon.
Perak JBPM Operations assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the body was found at 2pm, about four kilometres from the spot where he had jumped at Batu 18, Kampung Kuchai, near Bota Kiri.
“The search operation resumed this morning, involving 30 personnel, including the K9 Unit and Water Rescue Team (PPDA), within a six-kilometre radius along the river.
“The victim’s body was subsequently found floating by the PPDA team and brought ashore before being handed over to the police for further action,” he said in a statement today.
Earlier, Sabarodzi said the incident occurred at about 5pm yesterday when the man jumped into Sungai Perak to retrieve his boat. His nephew had attempted to rescue him, but the effort was unsuccessful. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar heads to India for BRICS summit, bilateral talks with world leaders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — After concluding his working visit to Sabah today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim departed for New Delhi to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, where he is also scheduled to hold several bilateral meetings.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said he was scheduled to meet the Prime Minister of India, as well as the presidents of Russia, Iran and Kazakhstan and the Prime Minister of Ethiopia.
“My delegation and I have departed for New Delhi, India to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit.
“My itinerary in India also includes a visit to Keralam to meet the Grand Mufti of India to exchange views on community development, education and religious affairs,” he said.
After completing his diplomatic mission in India, Anwar will proceed to Malé, Maldives for an official visit at the invitation of President Dr Mohamed Muizzu.
“May everything go smoothly and may this visit bring tangible benefits to the people and the country. Insya-Allah,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Past is past, but Umno delegates want PAS to prove it can be different
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Beside one of the ministry booths at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, Muhammad Awang stood with a friend and picked up a copy of
Utusan Malaysia
from a pile laid out for delegates as others milled around the Umno general assembly.
At 68, the Umno Kuala Krai division secretary has seen the party’s relationship with PAS shift from cooperation to rivalry and back again.
But as Umno now looks to forge a fresh understanding with its former political rival, Muhammad believes the past should not stand in the way of trying again.
“We have to put aside our respective egos. We have to be big-hearted,” he told Malay Mail on the sidelines of the assembly here.
Muhammad said any renewed cooperation between Umno and PAS would require both sides to make compromises, particularly over the allocation of seats in the next election.
“If it is Kelantan, we should give it to Umno. Elsewhere, we should also give seats to PAS. Let it be balanced,” he said.
PAS members attend the Umno Youth General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur yesterday. — Picture by Yusof Isa
His comments came as Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi called for greater political understanding between the country’s existing political coalitions in his speech at the assembly this morning.
Zahid revived his proposal for a “Grand Collaboration”, which he said was not about merging political parties but creating an understanding to avoid political clashes that could be damaging to all sides.
He described the political understanding as one based on prioritising common interests, respecting differences in ideology and identity, and practising tolerance and flexibility.
But he also stressed that political partners must not betray one another, warning against building an understanding during the day while plotting to bring down a partner at night.
For Muhammad, that warning is particularly relevant given Umno and PAS’ previous experience under Muafakat Nasional.
“Umno and PAS had Muafakat Nasional before, but it never reached the stage of being translated into an election. We did not have the chance to see it through.
“So we do not want to split for a second time. We have been separated several times and we do not want to be bitten by the same snake in the same hole,” he said.
Still, Muhammad said the previous breakdown should not prevent both parties from trying again.
He said both sides would need to put aside their egos and be willing to make concessions for the sake of Malay-Muslim unity.
For him, that meant accepting that neither side could expect to get everything it wanted, including when deciding which party should contest certain seats.
An Umno Kuala Lumpur delegate in his 60s, who declined to be named, similarly said PAS’ previous political decisions should be treated as a lesson rather than an obstacle to future cooperation.
“This is politics. We should do whatever can benefit Umno,” he said.
Delegates gather at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur for the 2026 Umno General Assembly on September 11, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Muhammad acknowledged that there had been what he described as many instances of betrayal, including PAS previously discussing Malay-Muslim unity with Umno before choosing to work with other political partners.
But he said he personally believed Umno and PAS should work together in the next general election.
“If we are divided, we are not strong. So I see this as a good step towards making the Malays and Muslims strong again,” he said.
Asked whether the past should now be left behind, he replied: “Yes, exactly. It is a lesson.”
He said he hoped the relationship now being built between Umno and PAS would not repeat the problems of their previous alliances.
The willingness to move on, however, does not appear to mean delegates have forgotten what happened before.
Selayang Umno Youth chief Shah Zanuriman Nuar Paras Khan, 40, speaks to Malay Mail on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur on September 11, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
For Shah Zanuriman Nuar Paras Khan, 40, the Selayang Umno Youth chief, rebuilding trust would require both sides to be clear about what they expect from one another.
“To avoid being betrayed, there needs to be a spirit of camaraderie, loyalty, mutual understanding and clear boundaries,” he said.
Shah added that the same stability delegates were looking for within Umno could also be important if the party were to work with other political partners.
“There are all sorts of disputes between the other parties. Bersatu is falling apart, then there are cracks here and there, and they are constantly fighting.
“Umno, meanwhile, remains stable. So I think that is what makes the people see Umno as remaining stable and maintaining its own momentum. There are no internal fights, no Camp A or Camp B, nothing like that.
“So perhaps the people are looking for stability amid an uncertain economic situation, and they see Umno as more stable than the other parties,” he said.
That balance between forgiveness and caution was also reflected in Zahid’s speech, where his call for political understanding was accompanied by a warning that agreements must be honoured.
Delegates said past political betrayals should serve as lessons rather than prevent Umno and PAS from working together again. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
The Umno president said political cooperation should allow parties to preserve their own identities, stressing that “Umno remains Umno” and “Barisan Nasional remains Barisan Nasional”.
For delegates like Muhammad, that may be the basis on which a new relationship with PAS can be built: not by pretending the past did not happen, but by deciding it should not dictate what comes next.
After years of political shifts between the two parties, he said it was time to try again with a more carefully negotiated understanding.

Title: Economy minister: Sabah receives RM582m, highest allocation for small-scale projects nationwide since 2023
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — A total of RM1.52 billion has been allocated for 8,069 small-scale projects and People’s Facility Initiatives (IKR) nationwide since 2023, with Sabah receiving the largest share at RM582.29 million for 2,301 projects.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said RM175.24 million of the allocation for Sabah was channelled for the implementation of 985 IKR projects, and RM407.05 million was for 1,316 small-scale projects.
For this year alone, he said, Sabah received RM113.3 million to implement 481 IKR and small-scale projects, out of a total national allocation of RM323.8 million.
“Every application must undergo an evaluation process to ensure the project is feasible, taking into account factors such as suitability, status and site availability, before funds are channelled to the implementing agencies,” he said.
He told reporters this after visiting an IKR project to upgrade a wooden bridge to a semi-concrete structure in Kampung Kalansanan here today.
On the need for concrete bridges in water-based settlements, particularly in Sabah, Akmal Nasrullah said the Ministry of Economy was considering making the construction of such facilities a priority under the IKR programme next year.
He said the matter warranted attention as bridges served not only as pathways for residents but were also important for safety, particularly during emergencies such as fires.
“For next year, under the IKR programme, we can make these small bridges a key focus area. When the ministry receives applications from residents or Sabah, we will prioritise these small bridge projects,” he said.
On the project he visited, Akmal Nasrullah said it was valued at RM199,508 and implemented by Kota Kinabalu City Hall (DBKK) under the IKR programme, and was completed on January 13.
He said the project involved upgrading a bridge measuring 200 feet (about 70 metres) in length and 1.8 metres in width to improve safety and facilitate the movement of residents. — Bernama

Title: GISBH fails in bid to challenge Kedah fatwa declaring teachings deviant
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 11 — The Alor Setar High Court has dismissed an application by GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) and its Chief Executive Officer, Nasiruddin Mohd Ali, for leave to initiate judicial review proceedings to challenge a state fatwa issued against them last year.
The fatwa, issued by the Kedah State Fatwa Committee on February 12 last year, ruled that the beliefs, teachings, tenets and practices of GISBH members and followers were deviant and contrary to Islamic teachings.
The committee also ruled that any Muslim who acted in contravention of the fatwa committed an offence under the Syariah Criminal Offences Enactment (Kedah Darul Aman) 2014 and was liable to legal action under the laws in force in Kedah.
Judge Evawani Farisyta Mohammad dismissed the application by GISBH and Nasiruddin after allowing the Attorney General’s objection to their application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings.
In the grounds of judgment dated September 7, which was uploaded on the judiciary’s website, the judge said the contents of the fatwa were based on Syariah law and therefore fell within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Syariah Court, meaning that the Civil Court had no jurisdiction to determine the matter.
“…this court, regarding the reliefs sought by the applicants (GISBH and Nasiruddin), is essentially being asked to review the content or substance of the fatwa and to quash it,” she said.
Judge Evawani also said the fatwa referred to individuals involved with GISBH rather than GISBH as a corporate entity.
She noted that the fatwa was issued pursuant to the prerogative powers of the Sultan of Kedah and was therefore a decision that was non-justiciable and could not be challenged through judicial review.
In their application for leave, GISBH and Nasiruddin had sought an order of certiorari to quash the decision made by the respondents through the issuance of the fatwa.
The applicants named the Kedah State Fatwa Committee, Kedah State Islamic Religious Council and Mufti of Kedah as respondents.
Nasiruddin and GISBH claimed that the fatwa had adversely affected their operations and reputation, as well as those of individuals associated with them, and had resulted in them being perceived as followers of deviant teachings.
The Attorney General objected to the application on the grounds that the fatwa was not subject to judicial review or adjudication, as it constituted an exercise of the Ruler’s prerogative powers. — Bernama

Title: Penang LRT works to close part of Jalan Magazine for 21 days from Sept 14
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 11 — Jalan Magazine here will be closed for 21 days from September 14 to facilitate road widening and utility relocation works for the LRT Mutiara Line project.
Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) said the closure would be in effect around the clock from 10pm on September 14 until 5am on October 5.
“The closure will involve the leftmost lane of Jalan Magazine in front of St. Giles Wembley Hotel heading towards KOMTAR, while the other lanes will remain open to traffic,” it said in a statement today.
It said a partial lane closure would also be implemented intermittently along Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah from 8am to 4pm daily from September 16 to December 15 to facilitate construction of the LRT Mutiara Line, including drainage and road widening works.
The closure will involve the leftmost lane between the Sunny Point Complex traffic light junction and the Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) field heading towards KOMTAR, as well as the rightmost lane in front of the USM field and Batu Uban Army Camp in both directions.
“Other lanes will remain open to traffic at all times. Road users are advised to exercise caution when passing through the area.
“Road signs and traffic cones will be placed, while flagmen will be deployed to help manage traffic flow and ensure the safety of road users at the affected routes,” it added. — Bernama

Title: Chief minister says Melaka election not far off, dissolution of DUN required by year‑end
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, September 11 — As talks and speculation on the upcoming Melaka state election intensify, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has hinted that the wait will be neither too long nor too soon.
Speaking to the press during the 2026 Umno General Assembly at World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL), Rauf said that that Melaka must dissolve its state legislative assembly (DUN) by the end of December as its five year term is nearing completion.
“Our efforts have been underway for the past two years.
“We are now merely waiting for the final curtain to fall on this work so we can dissolve the assembly.
“We can’t delay the dissolution of the DUN because the date is inching closer,” Rauf said.
When asked about the possible candidates, Rauf is keeping their identity pretty close to his chest however revealed that they are not closing the door for cooperation with other political parties if the people wants it.
When asked about the possible candidates, Rauf kept their identity pretty close to his chest, but shared that they are not closing the door to cooperation with other political parties if the people want it.
“We will leave it to the people to decide who the best strategic partner is for the Melaka state government.
“I have made it clear that any talks with political parties wishing to join the Melaka democracy stage will only happen once the DUN is dissolved,” Rauf said.
He added that he and his team will continue to fight for the 21 seats in Melaka that they’ve won previously and will not be compromising them for others.
“To contest is the right of any party, but we cannot compromise on the 21 seats we currently hold,” he said.
